Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Nebula Analytics - inference topology review & next steps

Thanks for taking the time today, Alex and Maria — good discussion. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the immediate asks, and our proposed next steps so everyone is aligned. Please flag anything we missed.

Key pain points (as described):
- Interactive tail latency spikes during peak traffic (user-facing search + chat workflows).
- High token spend from repeated long-context prompts; limited prefix/KV caching today.
- Batch analytics jobs create unpredictable contention on the serving pool.

Goals Nebula articulated:
- Keep p95 latency under ~150ms for interactive paths, p99 under ~350ms.
- Support a 2k token context for the tuned 13B model for product features.
- Run a 6-week POC demonstrating stable latency and a 30–40% token-cost reduction through caching/quantization.

Immediate asks (what we will provide):
1) Topology proposal (attached: redwood-topology-proposal.pdf) — candidate node types, pool sizing, and fallback variants.
2) Load-profile template (attached: nebula-load-profile.csv) — please populate with 72-hour traffic samples and 95/99 targets.
3) SLA matrix draft (attached: sla-matrix.xlsx) and a HubSpot deal link: HS-12784.

Action items & owners:
- Nebula (Alex/Maria): share 72-hour production traces + example prompts by Tue 2028-06-05.
- Redwood (Ben + Vivek): produce a topology cost/latency estimate and POC runbook by Fri 2028-06-02.
- Legal/Procurement (Nebula): share procurement timeline/POC purchase path; procurement@nebula-analytics.com copied in this thread.

Proposed POC outline (high level):
- Week 0: infra prep, model variant pinning, data access (redacted).
- Weeks 1–4: ingest traffic replay + live sampling, KV/prefix cache tuning, quantization experiments.
- Weeks 5–6: monitoring & Q&A, SLA verification, handoff notes.

Ben will follow up with a technical topology snapshot and configuration suggestions (GPU types, batch sizing, cache configuration) — he cc'd below.

Thanks — Vivek

--
Vivek Kulkarni

Thanks Vivek — that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side so the topology/cost estimate is realistic:

- SLO targets: interactive p95 target = 140–150ms; p99 target = 330–380ms (we can tolerate brief variance during heavy batch windows).
- Throughput profile: baseline ~120 reqs/min for interactive paths; peak burst to ~600 reqs/min during major reports. Batch analytics jobs run nightly and can be scheduled but will need bandwidth for 8–12 hour windows.
- Model: We plan to serve a custom fine-tuned 13B LLM (2k context). There is a fallback 7B distilled variant for low-cost queries. No external model hosting allowed — model weights will be provided via secure transfer (we control keys).
- Data residency: must remain in US-East for the POC.

Procurement note: procurement@nebula-analytics.com will coordinate the POC purchase order. They asked for a simple SOW and estimated spend band to review internally.

We will push a 72-hour trace dump and a sample prompt set by next Tuesday.

Appreciate the clear action list. — Alex

Subject: Technical topology snapshot & runbook (initial) — Nebula POC

Alex / Maria — following up with the technical sketch Vivek referenced. High-level notes first, then attachments and concrete asks.

Top-level proposal (short):
- Dedicated pool approach: 6–8 x A100 (80GB) equivalent GPUs for interactive tier (low latency, KV cache resident on GPU memory); a separate burst/batch pool sized at 4 x A10G for scheduled analytics jobs to keep contention isolated.
- Model variants: serve 13B FP16 (primary) + 7B quantized int8 fallback for cost-sensitive paths. We'll test GPT-like decoding optimizations and autoregressive kernel choices.
- Caching: Prefix/KV caching at the prefix level plus request-level LRU for repeated conversational contexts. Expected token reduction 25–35% depending on repetition.
- Batching policy: dynamic batching with a 10–25ms scheduling horizon for interactive; aggressive batching windows for batch jobs.
- Quantization experiments: 4-bit and 8-bit test runs in week 2 to trade throughput vs quality.

Estimated POC latency bands (initial sim):
- 13B FP16, no cache: p95 ~180ms (varies by sequence length), p99 ~420ms.
- 13B + prefix cache (warmed): p95 ~120–150ms, p99 ~300–350ms.
- 7B int8 fallback: p95 < 90ms, p99 < 160ms.

What we attached:
- nebula-load-profile.csv (template + example filled with synthetic traffic)
- sla-matrix.xlsx (SLO checklist + validation steps)
- redwood-topology-proposal.pdf (concise topology diagrams and recommended node types)

Concrete asks (to enable accurate sizing):
1) Share 72-hour production traffic dump (timestamps, request type tags, median/95/99 token lengths).
2) Provide samples of your fine-tuned model access method (S3 location or transfer plan) and key rotation policy.
3) Confirm expected live window for nightly batch jobs (start/end times).

Next steps:
- I will run a short local sim once we get the 72-hour dump and return a revised sizing by Fri 2028-06-02.
- If Nebula is comfortable, we can spin the POC in a dedicated US-East cluster and schedule the first replay in Week 1 of the POC.

Quick technical caveat: if the fine-tuned model uses custom ops, we may need a build step in our private runtime to ensure kernel support. Please flag that early.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
